rows.text: Ensure free/promotional Alia usage is still cost-attributed internally.
rows.evidence: CORRECTED, on a measurement from the workstream 12 agent that this audit got backwards. The audit said free and promotional usage "does write a `cost_entries` row, so cost attribution exists". IT DOES NOT. `recordCost` (lib/cost-tracker.ts:141) is the only wrapper of `insertCostEntry` and has ZERO non-test callers, so NOTHING is cost-attributed on the token-metered paths at all — free or paid — and `cost_entries` is empty in production while `getGlobalCostStats` returns zeros. That is why it was easy to miss: a correct read of an empty table and a broken switch look identical. Confirmed independently three ways, each re-runnable: the file comment at cost-tracker.ts:17 ("Nothing in this repository calls `recordCost`"); an AST census over `git ls-files -- packages/api/src` excluding tests and cost-tracker.ts itself, now standing as packages/api/src/__tests__/billingSeparation.test.ts:710-722 with the positive control that the same scan DOES find the symbol where it is defined; and routes/__tests__/v1-compatibility-surface.test.ts:655. The audit's SECOND clause was accurate and stands: routes/referrals.ts:89 and :93 credit a promotional referral reward with `addCredits(..., 'paid')`, so a grant and a purchase are indistinguishable at the balance layer.
rows.deliverable: DELIVERED IN PART by #175 (`61e66e73`), migrations applied to the alia database by that commit's deploy run. `cost_entries` and `voice_call_usage` both carry a `grant_kind` column with a CHECK rendered from packages/api/src/domain/credit-funding.ts:39 (`free_allowance` | `paid_balance`); `CreditReservation` carries `grantKind` (credits-manager.ts:40, decided at :134 from the balance the spend returned); `recordCost` accepts it; and the VOICE settlement writes it live (voice-session-manager.ts:1256) — the one settlement where a CreditReservation and the serving provider coexist, and where `voice_call_usage` is both the usage record and the billing figure.
rows.guard: packages/api/src/__tests__/billingSeparation.test.ts, "the token-metered ledger still has no writer, and this is the count that says so" — an exact-set assertion that goes RED the day `recordCost` gains a caller, which is precisely the day this row needs re-reading. It carries its own positive control (the scan finds `recordCost` in cost-tracker.ts) so an empty offender list means absence rather than a scan that read nothing.
rows.residual: THIS TICK IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and is recorded as one. It rests on two things: the voice settlement writing `grant_kind` live (voice-session-manager.ts:1256), and the standing assertion in billingSeparation.test.ts that goes red the day `recordCost` gains a caller. It is NOT whole-service coverage: on the token-metered paths nothing is attributed at all, free or paid, so the property holds there by ABSENCE. delivery.valueVersusBinding: THE LIKELIEST WRONG TURN, and it is half-right, which is what makes it dangerous. A secret reaches a container through THREE layers, and only the first is still deliverable: (1) the SSM parameter supplies the VALUE and is written by deploy-aws.yml's `sync_secret` step on every deploy — OPEN; (2) the task definition's `secrets[]` entry supplies the name->ARN BINDING and was delivered by oxy-infra at service CREATION, before `ignore_changes` had anything to ignore, and carried forward by CI ever since — CLOSED; (3) `environment[]` likewise — CLOSED. So writing /oxy/alia/ALIA_KAANA_CREDENTIAL_KEY into SSM DELIVERS NOTHING ON ITS OWN: nothing reads it, there is no error, and the deploy is green. TASK_SECRET_OVERRIDES_JSON is the only way CI can add a NEW binding. Keep declaring the bindings in oxy-infra regardless — that block's own comment gives the reason: "a live-but-undeclared secret is one apply from vanishing, and an unlisted one silently never syncs."

secrets.ALIA_KAANA_CREDENTIAL_KEY: kaana-credential.ts calls the pair "the secret material that proves the process is entitled to act as" the ApplicationCredential.
secrets.ALIA_KAANA_CREDENTIAL_SECRET: same; exchanged for a short-lived token and never present in a request.

configuration.ALIA_KAANA_CREDENTIAL_ID: the credential RECORD's id. kaana-credential.ts: it "rides on every request inside the contract's principal" — a value that travels in the envelope is not a secret.
configuration.ALIA_KAANA_ACCOUNT_ID: carried in principal.billing.accountId on every request.
configuration.ALIA_KAANA_APPLICATION_ID: carried in the principal on every request.
configuration.ALIA_KAANA_ENVIRONMENT: one of the contract's environment enum values.
configuration.ALIA_KAANA_INFERENCE_SCOPES: a comma-separated scope list, echoed in the principal.

secretVersusConfiguration.rule: Two secrets, eight configuration. Configuration belongs in environment[], not in an SSM SecureString: routing it through SSM is not wrong, it is more moving parts, and every entry added to secrets[] is a BINDING that cannot be delivered by any open route.

delivery.placeholderFootgun: `sync_secret` skips an empty value or a literal `-` with a ::warning:: and leaves SSM unchanged (deploy-aws.yml). The guard is right — it is what stops a placeholder overwriting a live value, after REDIS_URL=- crash-looped oxy-api — but it fails three different ways while staging a cutover in halves. `-` with NO parameter yet: sync skipped, deploy GREEN, next task launch fails ResourceInitializationError: unable to pull secrets. `-` with a parameter already there: sync skipped and the OLD value silently remains. A real-looking placeholder (TODO, changeme): no guard catches it and every model call ends in authentication_failed. The rule is the ecosystem one — if you do not have the real value yet, do not create the secret at all.

verdictHazards.greenAndInert: A mechanism can exist, be tested, and be called by nothing. Evidence that names a function, a config table or a module is not evidence that the property HOLDS unless the ENTRYPOINT calls it. Row 266 failed this way and is corrected above. Every ALREADY_TRUE and DUPLICATE_OF row was re-checked against it on 2026-08-17; the live callers are: reserved-namespace via gateway-client.ts:320, fallback-engine via gateway-client.ts:339, violatedCapability via kaana-client.ts:931 (client-internal only), and gates 3/4/5, which are censuses that run in CI. The two rows that hold by ABSENCE with NO guard at all are 454 and 522, and both now say so in their mutation field rather than naming a guard that does not cover them.
verdictHazards.wrongArtefact: Rows 266 and 654 were wrong in the same direction and neither was caught by this audit. 266 cited a mechanism nothing called; 654 cited an absence that was not absent, because the scan read headings rather than prose. Both are corrections to the same habit: measure the artefact the claim is about. A heading census answers "is there a section named X", never "is the rule written"; an import census answers "does this module exist", never "does the entrypoint call it".
verdictHazards.emptyTableReadsCorrect: Row 475 asserted that a write happened because the code path that would write existed. It did not: `recordCost` has no caller, so `cost_entries` is empty and every aggregate over it returns zero. A correct read of an empty table and a broken switch are indistinguishable without a positive control, which is why the standing gate for it carries one.
verdictHazards.ratchetNotSynchroniser: A synchronising process that only ever ADDS is not a synchroniser, it is a ratchet. This file's `resolvedSince` sync could mark a row resolved and never unmark it, so a re-opened box stayed "done" — and the epic read as further along than it was, which is the precise failure the file exists to prevent. Caught only because a count disagreed by one. Same family as a floor that a gate's own work erodes until it asserts nothing, and as a matrix row that outlives the file it names. The fix is always the same: make the check answer BOTH directions and assert the exact count, never a floor.
verdictHazards.typeSystemViaTextCensus: A census over source TEXT cannot answer a question about the TYPE SYSTEM. Found by the workstream 12 agent in #167's audit guard: packages/api/src/lib/security/__tests__/config-audit.test.ts:319 asserts no caller can omit the actor by testing `not.toMatch(/actor\?\s*:/)` — and a DEFAULT PARAMETER (`actor: ConfigAuditActor = {…}`) defeats it completely. There is no `?`, so the regex misses; the signature census still sees a parameter named `actor` typed `ConfigAuditActor`; and TypeScript treats it as optional at every call site. Proven rather than argued: a probe calling the writer with no actor typechecks with zero errors. This is the same family as `wrongArtefact` — a property enforced by the type system needs a gate IN the type system, or at minimum an AST check that reads the parameter's optionality rather than its spelling. L544 stays ticked: the mechanism holds, only that sub-property's coverage was hollow.
verdictHazards.mentionIsNotACall: A guard that survives its own mutation because an IMPORT LINE satisfies it. The workstream 4 agent's first version asserted models.tsx contains `useCatalogue`; replacing the hook call with a literal empty array SURVIVED, because the import statement still contained the identifier. A component can satisfy "imports X" while never calling X. Fixed by asserting `useCatalogue(` with the parenthesis. Sibling of greenAndInert and distinct from it: there the MECHANISM had no caller, here the ASSERTION could not tell a call from a mention.
verdictHazards.textCannotSeeAnInvertedCondition: A source-text entrypoint assertion cannot see an inverted condition. `expect(source).toContain('kaanaBlocksReadiness()')` proves the route NAMES the function, never that it acts on the answer — keep the call and invert to `if (!kaanaBlocksReadiness())` and the task reports not-ready exactly when Kaana IS reachable, with 1387 tests passing. Found by the workstream 8 agent; the box (394) was un-ticked. THE GENERALISATION MATTERS MORE THAN THE INSTANCE: src/index.ts is asserted only by source TEXT because nothing imports it — it opens a socket, arms timers and connects a database at import — so EVERY boot-path guard in this epic shares this shape and none of them can see a negation. The escape is the one kaana-boot-check.ts already took: put the decision in a FUNCTION that a test can call with an environment, and leave index.ts holding only the log line and the exit.
verdictHazards.emptyBecauseGated: An empty list from a gated endpoint and an empty store are the same bytes. `GET https://api.oxy.so/v1/models` returns `{"data":[],"count":0}` — which reads as "the catalogue is empty" and is actually "you are a PUBLIC viewer and INFERENCE_CATALOGUE_AUDIENCE is unset" (OxyHQ/oxy routes/inferenceCatalogue.ts states it in its own header). The re-audit therefore records the catalogue contents as UNMEASURED rather than as zero. Same family as `emptyTableReadsCorrect`: a correct read of a filtered view and a correct read of an empty one are indistinguishable without the credential that lifts the filter.
verdictHazards.liveIsNotServable: A green liveness probe and a fresh artefact prove the process is up and the credential is valid. Neither proves the thing behind it will answer. Kaana is 2/2, /livez is 200, and its publisher re-issued the inventory 14 minutes before it was read — and its only provider account answered 402 `payment_required` to every chat completion on the day it was measured, because the publisher reads /v1/models and the 402 arrives on /chat/completions. The cheap discriminator: ask which ENDPOINT the freshness signal exercised, not whether it is fresh.
verdictHazards.reachableIsNotAddressable: "The service exists and answers" and "this caller may use it" are different measurements, and the first is the one that is cheap. Kaana is reachable from anywhere; Alia still cannot call it, because it refuses anything that is not an Ed25519-signed Oxy edge envelope and holds only public keys. A re-audit that stopped at `curl /livez` -> 200 would have unblocked 96 rows onto a door Alia has no key to. The discriminator was one more request: `GET /internal/v1/health` -> 401 naming the envelope.
verdictHazards.taskDefinitionIsNotTheEnvironment: An ECS task definition's `environment[]` and `secrets[]` are not the whole of what a process can reach. oxy-alia:105 names no provider credential, which is evidence about variables and NOT about whether Alia holds provider keys: `provider_keys.key` is a Postgres column that key-manager.ts reads at request time. Reading the task definition and concluding "Alia holds no provider secret" measures the wrong artefact — the same habit as `wrongArtefact`, in an infrastructure currency.
verdictHazards.ownershipIsNotDelivery: A configuration file can be the right PLACE for a value and still be no route to production. oxy-infra owns Alia's ECS environment, and `ignore_changes = [task_definition]` plus a deploy script that re-renders from `services[0].taskDefinition` means a variable added there reaches nothing, forever, with no error and no drift alarm — while the PR that added it is green, reviewed and merged. The measurement that separates the two: read the RUNNING revision back, never the config. Positive control available on request — oxy-oxy-api:231 vs :232, seven minutes apart, where the Terraform PR is not what delivered the variables. Same family as `greenAndInert` one layer out: there the mechanism had no caller, here the declaration has no adopter.
verdictHazards.duplicateAssertsMore: A row labelled a duplicate can assert MORE than the row it duplicates, and the label then hides an OPEN requirement behind a TICKED one. `DUPLICATE_OF` was carrying four different relationships that read identically in this file and all resolve to a ticked primary: a genuine restatement; a CONJUNCTION whose components are mostly open (773, 24 of 46 open); an INVERSE, where the primary is a prohibition satisfied by doing nothing and the row demands the positive act (576); and a row about a DIFFERENT SURFACE from its primary (606 — `GET /catalogue` versus `/v1/*`). The discriminator is one question asked of the PAIR rather than of the label: would ticking the primary alone make this row’s sentence true? If the row names anything the primary does not, the answer is no and the verdict is wrong. Seven rows were re-classified on 2026-08-19 — 103, 576, 606, 647, 650, 768, 773 — and not one of them was a duplicate. Same family as `greenAndInert`: there the mechanism had no caller, here the evidence measures a different claim from the one the row makes.

toolingHazards.ghPrEditBodyFile: `gh pr edit --body-file` does NOT write the body on this repository. Measured first-hand on 2026-08-17 against PR #181: it exits **1** and prints, on stderr, `GraphQL: Projects (classic) is being deprecated ... (repository.pullRequest.projectCards)` — and the body is unchanged, confirmed by reading it back twice (4579 bytes before and after). Reported independently by three other agents on this epic before I reproduced it, so it is not a one-off. WHY IT GETS THROUGH: the failure is not silent, it is MISLABELLED. The error names Projects, not the body, so a human reads it as a harmless deprecation notice and moves on — and on #168 a PR carried a 186-character placeholder through review because of exactly that. THE WORKING PATH: `gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n> -F body=@<file>`, measured exit 0 with the new length returned. THE CHEAP DEFENCES, in order: check the exit code (it is non-zero, so `set -e` or an explicit check catches it), then read the field back — which is the general rule for `gh` writes in ~/AGENTS.md, and this is the instance that proves it. A SECOND TRAP MEASURED IN THE SAME SESSION: `gh pr view ... > body.md` truncates `body.md` BEFORE running, so a failed fetch leaves a 0-byte file that the next write would publish as an empty body. Only the no-op above prevented that here.
